articles.title_orig: China earthquake: Powerful quake collapses hundreds of homes in Tibet
articles.title_zh: China earthquake: Powerful quake collapses hundreds of homes in Tibet
articles.content_orig:
More than a dozen people were killed and hundreds of homes destroyed when a magnitude 7.0 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening local time, according to local officials.
The United States Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10:33 p.m. local time, with its epicenter 119 miles east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet.
At least 16 people were killed and 54 people were injured in the earthquake, Chinese state media said.
Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 35 sustained minor injuries, the media office said.
More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts. Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, around 3,000 tents and folding beds, as well as flashlights and winter clothing arrived in the region.
It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China's national broadcaster CCTV said.
Nagqu is more than 186 miles north of Tibet's capital, Lhasa.
The USGS put the earthquake's depth at 11 miles.  Xinhua, citing the China Earthquake Networks Center, put the depth at 6.2 miles.
The earthquake comes less than two months after a border region of Nepal and Tibet was struck by devastating flash flooding that left hundreds of people dead and destroyed several communities . Authorities said the flooding was caused by the collapse of a glacier.

articles.title_zh: Stock Market News, Oct. 22, 2026: Tech Selloff Deepens as Flight Into Treasurys Drives Yields Lower
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave is facing a crisis of confidence on Wall Street that's playing out in real time among equity and bond investors.
With interest rates spiking and AI build-out concerns mounting, debt-heavy neoclouds like CoreWeave are being viewed by many market participants as the most vulnerable trade in the artificial intelligence space.
"Sentiment is decidedly negative," Andrew Keches, a credit analyst at Barclays, wrote in a note to clients on Tuesday, referring broadly to corporate debt in tech. Keches highlighted the "speed at which AI vibes are shifting on a day-to-day basis."
CoreWeave, which went public in March of last year and reached a peak market cap of about $90 billion three months later, is now valued at roughly $31 billion, with its stock down 36% this month after plunging 10% on Thursday. Its unsecured debt, meanwhile, is sporting a yield of about 15%.
The spread on CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps, which are insurance against default, is up 179% in the past year and 39% in October. It last stood at 1,145 basis points, or 11.45%.
CoreWeave declined to comment.
The story is playing out across the neocloud sector. Shares of Nebius are down 33% this month, while IREN's stock is down 38%. In Australia, shares of data center operator NextDC plunged 40% on Wednesday after the company slashed its annual earnings forecast. Earlier this month, Australian data center company Firmus scrapped its planned initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions.
U.K. neocloud Nscale is now under the microscope as investors wait to see whether the Nvidia-backed company will go through with its IPO. The company filed to go public on the New York Stock Exchange last month.
A representative from Nscale declined to comment.
CoreWeave is the biggest of the pack, and is intimately tied to the U.S. AI market. Nvidia is its top institutional investor, with a stake of about 9%, according to FactSet. And more than two-thirds of CoreWeave's revenue last year came from Microsoft .
That's put a spotlight on CoreWeave's financials and its ability to remain viable. The company has about $20.7 billion in debt coming due through 2030 and another $14.9 billion thereafter, with the prospects of higher interest rates on future financing.
Sources on credit desks told CNBC that the high-yield debt market is effectively on hold until after the midterm elections in two weeks given ongoing concerns about the political pushback that data centers are facing. One source, who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the matter, said fixed income investors "want permitting and regulatory requirements to be substantially resolved" before they commit financing.
"Given recent turbulence, pausing makes sense," Seth Meyer, global head of client portfolio management at Janus Henderson, said in an interview.
CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator, who co-founded the company in 2017 initially as a crypto-mining venture, sent a memo to employees on Thursday, which CNBC obtained, to try and tamp down concern. Intrator stressed that the company maintains a range of funding options.
"Our financing model combines infrastructure-backed borrowing, corporate debt, equity, and customer prepayments," Intrator wrote. He added that the company has "additional flexibility to raise equity over time as market conditions and our capital needs warrant."
CoreWeave had $5.5 billion of cash and equivalents at the end of the second quarter. The company is expected to report third-quarter results next month. Analysts expect negative free cash flow in the period to swell to $10.1 billion, the highest since the company started reporting quarterly financials, according to FactSet.
One issue being debated heading into the report is how much more capital CoreWeave needs to raise. Rob Oliver, a software analyst at Baird, is estimating roughly $30 billion in 2027.
"Earnings may address financing measures to shore up confidence," Oliver said in an interview. "But they wouldn't need that capital until the first quarter."
Another question is whether Nvidia will step in if necessary?
Nvidia, which supplies the graphics processing units that CoreWeave rents out, invested $2 billion in January for a 10% stake. The purchase price was $87.20 a share. The stock is now trading at $61.82 even after jumping 6% the day of the announcement.
While Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said last week that CoreWeave doesn't need a backstop, some investors say the chip giant's further participation may be necessary if credit conditions continue to worsen.
Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
Analysts at Goldman Sachs , JPMorgan Chase and Barclays have put out bullish notes on the company this week, highlighting the company's GPU-backed loans and its solid list of investment-grade customers like Microsoft and Meta . Goldman analysts emphasized the company's strength in the market relative to many of its neocloud competitors.
"Not all neoclouds are created equal," they wrote, in upgrading their rating to buy from hold. "CoreWeave is likely in the top quartile of neoclouds, if not the top decile, when measured on performance and ability to execute."
— CNBC's Michelle Fox and Jordan Novet contributed to this report.

Local authorities have found at least two people injured in a village near the epicentre, with some houses in villages closest to the epicentre showing cracks, according to Xinhua.
Videos released by local state media showed people leaving their ⁠homes and seeking shelter outside or in ⁠their cars parked on the street.

articles.title_orig: SK Hynix says Solidigm drops plan for US IPO amid market volatility
articles.title_zh: SK Hynix says Solidigm drops plan for US IPO amid market volatility
articles.content_orig:
Shares of South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix's were down as much as 3% in Seoul on Friday morning after the company halted a review of a potential U.S. initial public offering for its subsidiary Solidigm.
"Solidigm will halt its review of potential pre-IPO and IPO options," the company said in the statement after assessing recent capital market conditions and share price trends, while also exploring various funding options to finance a new U.S. semiconductor fabrication plant amid growing demand for AI memory.
The chip manufacturer said an IPO could have helped fund Solidigm's expansion while providing greater financial flexibility for shareholder returns, including dividends, share buybacks and share cancellations.
However, financial market volatility had increased and contributed to a broader correction in semiconductor stocks, prompting SK Hynix to reassess whether an IPO would benefit existing shareholders.
The company also said that Solidigm's existing production facilities had limited capacity to meet rising AI-driven memory demand, underscoring the need for additional manufacturing capacity in the U.S.
The decision also follows regulatory scrutiny in South Korea.
The country's financial regulator said Monday that a potential U.S. listing of Solidigm could violate South Korean rules restricting dual listings, according to Reuters.
Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin said regulators were examining whether the IPO would require a review under the country's rules designed to protect minority shareholders.
SK Hynix said Solidigm's investment needs remain unchanged and that it would continue exploring alternative financing options to support the subsidiary's growth and enhance shareholder value.
The announcement comes as U.S. technology stocks face pressure amid worries over AI spending.The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slid 2.6% on Thursday, its worst session since June, while Nvidia fell 4.4% and Advanced Micro Devices dropped 8.1%.
Amid a sell-off in memory stocks, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC Thursday that he does not expect an oversupply of memory chips by 2029, despite concerns over weakening demand.
AI data center stocks have also come under pressure amid growing concerns over financing risks and the pace of AI infrastructure expansion. Shares of CoreWeave plunged 10% on Thursday, extending their monthly decline to 36%, while Australia's NextDC tumbled nearly 40% on Wednesday after cutting its earnings forecast.

articles.title_orig: Switch 2 jailbreak gives hackers new ways to run homebrew and mod games
articles.title_zh: Switch 2 jailbreak gives hackers new ways to run homebrew and mod games
articles.content_orig:
A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining “userland” access that he says “lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO.”
The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4 , the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called “tethered” hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.
Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI’s Codex to poke at SmileBasic’s language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After “substantial effort for ~2 weeks,” that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.
From there, Hajhamid writes that he started poking around for access to the Switch 2’s internal sysmodules, looking for ones that could provide more privileged access to the console’s core functions. Eventually, he found a buffer overflow in the console’s FileSystem services module that exposed a cached data pointer, granting arbitrary read and write privileges. From there, Hajhamid writes that he could execute “privileged filesystem actions” and eventually achieve native code execution through a faked filesystem process.
Hajhamid, who goes by Pepsipu online, showed off a host of new modded characters in Mario Kart World as a proof of concept for the exploit. Others are similarly showing off simple demos and in-progress developer tools running on exploited hardware.
Full Vulkan GPU working in userland by u/Icy-ConcentrationC in switch2hacks
Still, the current “userland” exploit keeps any Switch 2 homebrew developers trapped in a relatively small sandbox, and falls well short of the kernel-level access that would provide full control of the hardware.
If the SmileBasic name sounds familiar to you, it’s probably because the 3DS version of the same software was key to the so-called smilehax exploit on that handheld back in 2016. Nintendo removed SmileBasic from the 3DS eShop shortly after that hack became public, and SmileBasic 4 has similarly already been delisted from the Switch eShop worldwide (though a Japanese demo version that may work similarly is still accessible as of this story’s publication).
That delisting could help slow the spread of this exploit to the wider base of Switch 2 owners that haven’t previously purchased and/or downloaded SmileBasic. But others in the Switch 2 hacking community are already teasing some similar exploits that appear to work using other games. And while the current exploit works on the latest Switch 2 firmware version (23.0.1), this particular vulnerability seems likely to be patched out in imminent firmware releases, which will be required for continued access to many Nintendo services and future game releases.
So while this exploit is definitely unwelcome news for Nintendo, it’s not nearly as problematic as the “unpatchable” original Switch exploit that surfaced in 2018 . That hack required a complete hardware redesign to ensure that future systems were not susceptible.
Still, the fact that Switch 2 hackers have gotten this far just over a year after the console’s release is not a good sign for the overall impregnability of Nintendo’s system software. Get ready for another never-ending cycle between console hackers and the hardware makers trying to keep them out of their console’s deepest recesses.

articles.title_orig: Moderna, Merck shares fall on eagerly anticipated cancer vaccine results
articles.title_zh: Moderna, Merck shares fall on eagerly anticipated cancer vaccine results
articles.content_orig:
A regimen involving the vaccine cut the risk of relapse or death by 42% in a landmark melanoma study that met investor expectations but triggered a “sell-the-news” response, one analyst wrote.
A cancer vaccine developed by Moderna and Merck & Co. has lived up to its billing, meeting lofty expectations from industry watchers and physicians in slowing the return of advanced melanoma, according to data published ahead of a major medical meeting.
Moderna and Merck reported in August that a combination of the vaccine, “intismeran autogene,” and Merck’s immunotherapy Keytruda, bested Keytruda alone in a late-stage trial. That study evaluated both regimens in the “adjuvant” setting after surgical removal of a tumor.
The companies didn’t disclose details from the trial at the time, only noting that the combination had met its main goal at an early, pre-planned data check. Nonetheless, the results were hailed by analysts as a “landmark moment” and evidence that intismeran is destined for billions of dollars in sales. Moderna’s stock price swelled more than four-fold afterwards.
The announcement made a coming Saturday presentation from the trial at the European Society for Medical Oncology meeting this year one of the biotechnology sector’s most eagerly anticipated. Ahead of it, Wall Street investors expected the intismeran regimen to be associated with anywhere from 40% to 50% relative reduction in the risk of disease recurrence or death.
Moderna had already stated a 35% lowering would constitute a clinically significant outcome, which itself was a high bar considering Keytruda alone hit the 43% mark when compared to a placebo.
Screenshots of the findings were leaked on social media Thursday, prompting ESMO to immediately release the closely guarded study details before the meeting. According to those findings, intismeran met its mark, as the combination cut the relative risk of disease recurrence or death by 42% compared to Keytruda alone after a median of 24.6 months.
The results fall a touch short of the 44% figure initially observed in a smaller and similarly closely watched Phase 2 trial. Long-term results from that study were even more profound, showing that the risk of relapse was nearly cut in half after five years of follow-up.
Shares of both companies immediately fell on the news, with Moderna’s stock price tumbling by nearly 25% and Merck’s by around 1%.
Some analysts immediately rallied to both companies’ defense. A “sell-the-news reaction is playing out,” wrote William Blair analyst Myles Minter. The findings "represent a highly compelling efficacy profile and substantially clear the [physician]-defined bar for a practice-changing dataset in adjuvant melanoma,” added TD Cowen analyst Tyler Van Buren.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Trung Huynh, however, noted that the results were on the “low end” of expectations and showed a "deterioration" from what was seen in earlier testing.
“While approval seems likely, commercial success is far less certain,” Huynh wrote.
Investigators interviewed by BioPharma Dive argued that the data represent a possible step forward in care for a persistent type of cancer.
Even with the availability of Keytruda — one of the most successful cancer drugs in history — one-third or more of people diagnosed with late-stage melanoma will die or see their disease return within five years of treatment. Drugmakers have struggled mightily to improve upon those numbers, with “PD-1” inhibitors like Keytruda as well as other medications.
“We have tried really hard. I have led clinical trials. None of them has improved over PD-1,” said Hussein Tawbi, a professor of medicine at the MD Anderson Cancer Center and an investigator in Moderna and Merck’s study. “We were resigned to the fact that this was the best we can do for patients. And now we see we can do better.”
Adding intismeran to Keytruda also reduced the relative risk of cancer spreading to “distant” organs or tissues by 38% versus Keytruda alone, researchers found.
The trial enrollees who got intismeran reported similar rates of side effects, although those recipients had a substantially higher frequency of fever and injection-site pain. About 7% of the people who got intismeran discontinued treatment because of an adverse event, compared with 5% of those in the comparator group.
The risk of these side effects is likely “something a lot of patients would be willing to take on” given their chance to live longer, said Janice Mehnert, director of melanoma and cutaneous medical oncology at NYU Langone Health. Mehnert was also involved in the study.
The results are the product of decades of research into vaccines that can train the body’s immune system to better recognize and hunt down cancer cells. Several earlier projects failed because they didn’t trigger a strong enough immune response, stimulated the wrong immune cells or couldn’t overcome tumors’ ability to thwart the body’s defenses. But more recently, developers like Moderna have turned to mRNA technology popularized by COVID-19 vaccines to come up with a newer approach.
This strategy is known as “individualized neoantigen therapy.” It involves sequencing a patient’s tumor to find cancer-specific protein flags, or “neoantigens,” and then delivering into cells mRNA that encodes for them. Their presence sparks a response from immune defenders called T cells to hunt down and destroy any cells with those proteins.
Intismeran teaches the body to spot up to 34 neoantigens. Another developer, BioNTech, has an individualized therapy in testing in colorectal and pancreatic cancer.
Moderna and Merck have now shown the approach can work in melanoma. But physicians and investors aren’t yet sure how broadly impactful it might be in other types of cancer or in earlier stage disease. BioNTech recently reported that its personalized vaccine failed a mid-stage trial in colorectal cancer.
Merck and Moderna are running additional studies in lung, bladder and kidney cancer. Interim results from a mid-stage trial in kidney tumors could come later this year or in the first half of 2027, RBC analyst Huynh recently wrote in a note to investors.

articles.title_orig: Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis
articles.title_zh: Hackers appear to be struggling to exploit PHP flaws after global cybersecurity crisis
articles.content_orig:
One day after governments around the world warned that newly publicized software vulnerabilities were so severe that websites should consider going offline until they could fix them, experts and insiders said there are few, if any, reports of widespread damage.
That could still change, of course, and cybersecurity experts warn that the threat will remain for weeks, if not longer. Still, there were early signs Thursday that hackers were finding it difficult to capitalize on the vulnerabilities.
“Across all our telemetry, and we are looking hard, we have only seen a couple of real exploitation attempts,” said Don Smith, vice president of threat research at the British software security firm Sophos.
Experts agree that that was in part because of a behind-the-scenes, global effort that identified the flaw and quietly designed a fix to address it.
The effort was aided, inadvertently, by the current limits of some widely available AI models, which did not appear to be very helpful at exploiting the vulnerabilities. And perhaps, they said, a little bit of luck.
“My sense is that these [vulnerabilities] are harder to exploit than folks thought at first, so this could be a slow burn,” Smith said.
The flaws were in PHP, a website programming language that is used in an estimated 69% of all websites. After researchers quietly found two devastating software vulnerabilities in August, they worked across borders and disciplines to develop patches that were released to the world Wednesday morning.
That led to an unusual circumstance in which government agencies from the FBI and the National Security Agency to European cybersecurity authorities and Australian intelligence agencies all recommended that websites go dark until they could implement the patches. And dozens of major websites around the world did just that.
Experts say there is plenty of evidence that hackers have been relentlessly scanning the flaws for ways to use them to attack targets.
But researchers and spokespeople from nine industry-leading companies — CrowdStrike, ESET, Google Threat Intelligence Group, Huntress, Palo Alto Networks, Recorded Future, SecureWorks, Sophos and Trail of Bits — told NBC News that as of Thursday evening, they had not seen any successful attacks.
“We have not yet seen these PHP vulnerabilities exploited in the wild yet,” said Sherrod DeGrippo, vice president of threat intelligence at Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42.
“We have seen over 200 examples of proofs-of-concept exploit code, and we’re actively investigating them all,” she said, referring to programs that claimed they could exploit the PHP flaws. “Whether or not there are current, active exploits is only a matter of time.”
While the vulnerability itself was devastating in theory, it was also technically very difficult to hack, said Dan Guido, CEO of the cybersecurity research and consulting firm Trail of Bits.
Guido said it took one of his employees, a 10-year veteran, an entire day to hack the vulnerabilities with an advanced AI model.
Amazon Web Services said it used honeypots — fake websites that cybersecurity researchers set up to trick and monitor hackers — to find evidence that hackers were trying to exploit the PHP vulnerability at least four days before it was made public.
“Technical analysis is ongoing, and it’s unclear if any of these attempts would have succeeded in real-world systems,” the company said in a blog post .
Matthew Prince, the CEO of Cloudflare, one of the internet’s most popular hosting companies, said that the company had been in talks for months about how to patch the flaw and that none of his customers were affected.
“The scary thing here is that something could have gotten compromised very quietly,” he said. “There may not be any public evidence that the server was compromised, and the hacker could just be hanging out there.”
While dormant intruders are always a potential threat in any hacking scenario, Guido, of Trail of Bits, said it was important to keep in mind that it takes more than just an experimental code and a little luck to hack a sophisticated web property.
That is especially true for hackers who rely on open-weight AI models — ones they can tinker with and remove guardrails from to assist with their operations.
Those models are not as powerful as those available to front-line cybersecurity researchers — and they typically struggle with complicated vulnerabilities like the PHP flaws.
“A lot of people are confusing proof of concept with exploit,” he said. “Turns out that writing exploits still requires expertise. You can’t just fake it.”
Kevin Collier is a reporter covering cybersecurity, privacy and technology policy for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Treasury yields log biggest drop since the 2023 banking crisis. Here’s what’s going on.
articles.title_zh: Treasury yields log biggest drop since the 2023 banking crisis. Here’s what’s going on.
articles.content_orig:
Treasury yields fell sharply on Thursday, with investors turning to safe havens amid a steep sell-off in stocks driven by concerns around the artificial intelligence trade and surging oil prices.
The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield — used to price mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — slid more than 17 basis points to 4.972%, the first time below 5% since Sept. 23. The yield saw its biggest one-day decline since March 10, 2023.
The yield on the 2-year Treasury note , which closely tracks short-term Federal Reserve rate policy, tumbled more than 16 basis points to 4.659%. The yield on longer-dated 30-year U.S. Treasury — most sensitive to geopolitical developments — was more than 14 basis points lower at 5.296%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
"It is a flight to safety," said Mitch Goldberg, president of ClientFirst Strategy. "People are all of a sudden terrified of the amount of bond issuance by AI-related companies. They see the rates going up and people want to hold on to something that they think will be there at maturity."
Others on Wall Street also sought to explain the turnaround in bond prices.
"For the first time in a while, Treasurys are enjoying haven status," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager for fixed income at Catalyst Funds. "You have weakness in tech, an escalation of risk in the Middle East and higher oil. On a relative basis Treasurys start to look like the safe place to hide again in the short term."
The reversal in bonds this week emerged as questions persisted about the billions being spent to build artificial intelligence networks.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC Thursday that while demand for neoclouds is " off the charts ," capital was scarce. Neoclouds are a specialized cloud computing providers that focus on high-performance tech infrastructure designed specifically for artificial intelligence.
This week's rebound in Treasury prices marks a turnaround from earlier this month, when 10- and 30-year yields reached their highest levels in more than two decades amid investor concern over inflation and high energy prices.
Above 5%, however, attitudes began to shift and yields suddenly starting looking like an attractive entry point, compensating even for the risk of inflation above 3%.
Tensions in the Middle East added to risk-off behavior Thursday. Oil prices moved sharply higher, with West Texas Intermediate futures closing up 2.39% at $99.47 per barrel. Brent crude futures, the global price benchmark, jumped 4%, rising to $113.17 a barrel.
Higher energy prices followed a New York Times report, citing unnamed U.S. officials, that the U.S. and Israel are considering resuming strikes on Iran in a "short but intensive" operation following the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
"You always look for one risk point, and there isn't really just one at the moment, which makes it a little bit more challenging," said Gregory Faranello, head of U.S. macro strategy at South Street Securities. "But if I had to take one of those and say what's most important right now, it has to be what's going on geopolitically."
"The consumer is clearly getting pinched here in the U.S., so it becomes tricky for central bankers" setting monetary policy going forward, he said. If energy prices "stay elevated, it could force the Fed's hand to do even more, which certainly wouldn't be wouldn't be a good thing for the bond market."
— CNBC's Michelle Fox contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: YouTube removing ‘Subscriptions’ bottom bar tab on Android, iOS after nearly a decade
articles.title_zh: YouTube removing ‘Subscriptions’ bottom bar tab on Android, iOS after nearly a decade
articles.content_orig:
YouTube is making a number of changes to its Android and iOS apps with the launch of custom feeds , including moving Subscriptions out of the bottom bar.
On mobile, YouTube is “kicking off a series of updates to shape a more seamless Home experience.” This starts with a redesigned top bar with dedicated feeds.
As part of this change, YouTube is removing the Subscriptions tab from its fourth position in the bottom bar. It’s now in the “top bar on the Home tab.” Testing of the redesign started earlier this year.
“Subs” appears in the second position after “Home” with a red underline that will take some getting used to. This change will break a lot of muscle memory, with Subscriptions appearing in the YouTube bottom bar for nearly a decade (2017).
Meanwhile, after Subs, you’ll see new dedicated feeds for Live, Music, and Movies & TV, with the latter only appearing if you have active subscriptions (such as Primetime Channels ). This change has the upside of removing YouTube’s navigation drawer.
They removed the only button I actually used.
More broadly, this change coincides with the launch of custom feeds, which are also available on and sync to the web. This lets you describe “what you want to see in your own words”.
Tap “+” at the top of your Home feed and describe the topic, channels, or vibe you’re looking for (for example, “help me unwind after work with guided meditations under 10 minutes”). You’ll then get a new feed tailored to your interests for you to explore.
They will appear as top tabs in the main feed after Home and Subs so that “you can jump back into them whenever you want.” The prompt box at the top of each feed lets you change it.
Notably, free users “can save up to 3 active custom feeds, while YouTube Premium members can save up to 8.”
Custom feeds are first rolling out on “mobile and desktop in English to U.S. based, signed-in viewers.” It will be available in more countries going forward.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Expands Satellite Cooperation With Finland, Signs 7 Deals Worth Nearly €300M
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Expands Satellite Cooperation With Finland, Signs 7 Deals Worth Nearly €300M
articles.content_orig:
In brief: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Thursday, Oct. 22 that he signed seven agreements with Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo, including deals to expand Kyiv’s use of Finnish satellite capabilities through Nokia and ICEYE. The total value of the agreements amount to over €300 million (roughly $337 million), as Ukraine and Europe weigh alternatives to Starlink that disrupted Ukrainian drone operations without prior warning.
Ukraine signed seven agreements with Finland, including deals to expand Kyiv’s use of Finnish satellite capabilities through Nokia and ICEYE after recent Starlink disruptions exposed how much of the country’s defense hinges on a single private provider that can restrict service with no prior warning.
President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the agreements in a statement on Thursday, Oct. 22, after holding discussions with the government of Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo. The documents, signed at the Ukrainian-Finnish Business Forum, outlines possible cooperation in defense production, rail transport, energy and housing construction, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We agreed that we will make greater use of Finland’s satellite capabilities,” Zelensky said. “This is important for our defense and for Ukraine’s resilience.”
The total estimated value of today’s agreements is nearly €300 million (roughly $337 million).
Among the agreements, Finland committed to hand over 10 Dv12 diesel locomotives and spare parts to Ukraine’s state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, free of charge.
Rail transport has become one of Ukraine’s most vital lifelines, with the country’s airspace closed to civilian flights from February 2022. Ukrainian citizens heavily rely on trains for travel, and the railway also carries critical cargo, including food shipments, across the country, making it a frequent target for Russian forces.
According to Koretskyi, Finland has become the first country to donate locomotives to Ukraine free of charge.
Earlier this week, Estonia has confirmed it will send a substantial number of locomotives to Ukraine. Although Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha did not provide additional information on the shipment, he said on Tuesday, Oct. 20, that during talks with Estonia, he had “outlined our urgent needs to strengthen Ukraine’s defense and resilience ahead of winter, with a particular focus on Russian strikes against our railways”
The appeal for railway help initially came mid-September, when Sybiha urged allies to provide Ukraine with replacement locomotives after a Russian strike hit a railway infrastructure just kilometers from the Polish border in Volyn region , in what may have been a deliberate attack on a train carrying diplomats .
Western allies were asked in particular to assist in finding locomotives compatible with the 1,520-milimeter railway gauge Ukraine uses, as well as provide funding to accelerate the procurement of new ones.
Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in 2022, Russia has damaged or destroyed more than 500 locomotives, with over half of those losses recorded this year alone, according to Sybiha’s estimates.
Mykola Kalashnyk, Ukraine’s Minister for Restoration, Infrastructure and Transport said on Aug. 23 that Russia has attacked Ukraine’s railway infrastructure at least 1,534 times so far in 2026.
Ukrainian drone manufacturers are also exploring expanding joint production with Finnish companies on Finnish soil, Koretskyi said.
Separately, employers’ associations from the two countries plan to establish a Ukrainian-Finnish Industrial Council, while another project focuses on industrial housing construction.
The two governments also agreed to share experience in protecting critical infrastructure and discussed Ukraine’s need for mobile shelters.
Meanwhile, Kyiv invited Finland to join its War Risk Insurance Fund.
“We expect Finnish companies to become key investors and long-term partners of Ukraine,” Koretskyi said. “Together, we can create products, technologies and businesses that will be competitive in Ukraine and across Europe.”
Ukraine’s large unused gas storage capacity and developed gas transmission system were on the agenda as well, with the two sides discussing how they could help Europe build strategic non-commercial gas reserves.
The discussions come as the EU works to cut off Russian gas entirely.
According to the European Commission , the EU’s dependency on gas imported from Russia has fallen from 45% of total imports to 12% in 2025, while all imports of Russian coal have been banned under EU sanctions.
“The remaining 35 billion cubic meters of Russian gas still imported to the EU annually will be out of our markets in less than two years,” the EC said on its official website.
In January 2026, EU member states gave final approval to a law banning Russian gas imports by late 2027, despite opposition from Hungary and Slovakia, both of which remain heavily reliant on Russian energy.
Under the law, imports of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) will end by the end of 2026, and pipeline gas by Sept. 30, 2027. According to The Baltic Times , Brussels built the ban on trade and energy legislation rather than sanctions, which require unanimity, so that it could not be blocked by Budapest and Bratislava.
The agreements with Finland come as Ukraine and its European partners search for alternatives to Starlink, the satellite service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Overnight on Oct. 13-14, speed restrictions were imposed on Starlink terminals without prior warning, crippling Ukraine’s drone operations. The limits disrupted several types of drones Ukraine uses to defend itself against Russian attacks, including interceptor drones deployed against jet-powered Shaheds.
The connectivity was lost on terminals moving at roughly 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) or faster, while Ukraine needed the operating speeds to reach at least 450 kilometers per hour (280 miles per hour).
The restrictions coincided with a reported week-long suspension of US intelligence sharing, which left Kyiv without allied warnings of Russian ballistic missile attacks.
Zelensky has accused those responsible of deliberately restricting the service during Russian attacks , saying the disruption weakened Ukraine’s defenses and, by doing so, endangered civilians.
After meeting senior US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday, Oct. 20, Zelensky confirmed the intelligence sharing had resumed . He added that progress on Starlink restrictions and Patriot interceptors could come within 48 hours.
Separately on Thursday, US Vice President JD Vance said Musk should not be at the center of the dispute over restrictions on Ukraine’s satellite service, framing the issue instead as a matter of US policy toward Russia’s war.
“Well, I think that fundamentally Elon Musk runs a private corporation, and I think it’s completely understandable that he doesn’t want to get in the middle of what is a war between two state actors without the US government effectively directing him on what to do,” he said, leaving unanswered who ordered the restrictions.
Both Musk and the White House denied responsibility for the restrictions, while pinning the blame to the other.
Meanwhile, the European Union is negotiating Ukraine’s access to its secure satellite communications program that could expand the system with commercial services in early 2027.
Currently, Europe has no ready-made replacement that Ukrainian troops can immediately attach to their drones and political pressure to develop alternatives is growing.

articles.title_orig: Zuckerberg makes deal with Meta to help him pay billionaire tax if it passes
articles.title_zh: Zuckerberg makes deal with Meta to help him pay billionaire tax if it passes
articles.content_orig:
Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.
The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (Â£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1% , external each year.
Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.
Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday , Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.
Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."
The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.
After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
Layoffs have continued into this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion , external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres .
Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.
It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.
And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

Global pharmaceutical firm AstraZeneca said on Thursday it would start selling a cancer drug after coming under criticism for failing to bring it to the US market faster, prompting some Americans to fly to Shanghai to procure the potentially life-saving medicine first developed by China.
In recent months, desperate Americans have travelled to China to obtain the Chinese-made cancer drug that was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration but remained unavailable in the country for more than a year, according to a cancer-treatment awareness advocate who made the journey while his mother was battling the disease.
Developed by China’s Dizal Pharmaceutical, sunvozertinib is a targeted lung cancer drug designed to treat adults with an advanced form of the illness, offering another treatment option for patients.
“The drug was approved in China in 2023. The FDA approved it in July 2025,” Max Doppelt, chief executive of Patient Data Vault, a consultancy that connects cancer patients to clinical trials, wrote on social media on Wednesday.

Rosneft officials are concerned that even a few more months of the war in Ukraine could cause lasting damage to the company’s business, Bloomberg reported, citing sources.
The company’s finances are deteriorating as profits fall and debt rises, Bloomberg’s sources said, despite expectations that the war in the Middle East would boost its earnings.
Rosneft has suffered significant damage from Ukrainian strikes on its oil refineries. The company operates 12 refineries that account for about a third of Russia’s total refining capacity. According to Bloomberg’s tally, five of the 15 confirmed drone strikes on Russian refineries in September alone targeted Rosneft facilities that supply fuel to European Russia.
The Ryazan refinery, which has repeatedly come under attack, is among the hardest hit. The Syzran refinery has spent most of the past six months either shut down completely or operating at less than a third of capacity. The Tuapse refinery has been shut down since April.
Bloomberg reported that Rosneft managed to restart some refineries within weeks of an attack, only for them to be struck again once repairs were complete or nearly complete. The constant need for repairs is driving costs to levels that cannot be sustained in the long run, the outlet’s sources said. As a result, they said, some plants have deliberately slowed repairs, stretching work that would normally take a few days into weeks.

articles.title_orig: Airbnb guests no longer have to wash the dishes or strip the beds at checkout
articles.title_zh: Airbnb guests no longer have to wash the dishes or strip the beds at checkout
articles.content_orig:
Airbnb hosts are melting down over a new policy banning them from making guests complete tasks that “would typically be performed by a cleaner,” like “stripping the bed, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes.”
The change, which applies to all bookings made on or after November 20, quickly sparked outrage after it was announced in an email to Airbnb hosts on Wednesday. Many began fuming online about losing the right to make their guests clean up after themselves.
“As hosts, we have a responsibility to protect our investments, our homes, and, in many cases, our personal living spaces,” one person wrote in Airbnb’s official forum for hosts. “The problem is that Airbnb increasingly expects hosts to accept the risks while limiting our ability to protect ourselves.”
“Airbnb is like an abusive partner,” wrote one user on the Reddit community r/airbnb_hosts. “I'm alive long enough to recognize how truthful those few words are,” another person replied . “Until and unless I see substantive changes, I'm finally out.”
A different self-described host declared that going forward, the kitchens in their rentals will be “stripped down to only bare essentials.”
Many guests, meanwhile, are celebrating. For years, travelers have complained about having to pay hefty cleaning fees as part of their Airbnb bookings, only to be required to complete a list of chores before checking out.
“The guest experience has become total ass,” one person said in a subreddit for Airbnb hosts. “Clean dishes and run in the dishwasher. Strip the beds, put all linen in the laundry room. Take out all garbage, put in garbage can, take to the curb. Honestly, knock it off.”
Airbnb noted in its Wednesday announcement that hosts can’t get around the new policy by putting cleaning tasks in the “Requests” section of their listings instead. Airbnb spokesperson Simon Letouze tells WIRED that hosts can still make “reasonable” requests, such as asking guests to put dirty dishes in the sink. Other examples Airbnb cites include asking guests to take short showers in areas with drought-related water restrictions, or telling them to place trash in bear-proof containers.
In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted what they claimed was a screenshot of their failed attempt to edit their property’s “Requests” section. They tried to ask guests to wash and air-dry dishes, put dirty towels in the laundry room, and take trash to a dumpster at an RV park they could find using a map on the refrigerator. But they realized they couldn’t hit Save. Airbnb's interface had underlined and highlighted the requests in red and displayed a pop-up that read “Guests shouldn't be asked to do this task.”
Hosts also can’t circumvent the new policy by giving guests a printed list of rules and asking them to sign it when they check in. On November 20, Airbnb is also banning hosts from requiring guests to sign separate contracts, with limited exceptions for local legal requirements, longer stays, or accessing “an optional amenity” like a “golf cart rental.”
If one of these situations applies, hosts have to mention it in the dedicated section of their listing. Airbnb adds that it “doesn’t help enforce the terms of these contracts.” Hosts who violate either policy, Airbnb warns, may receive warnings, or in severe situations, have their listings removed or be banned from the platform entirely.
In a Facebook group for Airbnb hosts, one person posted a letter they claimed to have sent to company executives, demanding the ability to set their own “common-sense expectations” for guests. They encouraged others to send their own versions. Another asked if they should raise their prices, while a third called for hosts to organize a platform-wide strike.
“Even if we all unlist our properties for just a day or two, we can send a powerful message,” they wrote. “Airbnb built its empire on OUR properties. It’s time we reminded them who actually holds the power.”
Some hosts haven’t given up on finding a way to ignore or get around the changes. On Reddit, one person said they would simply move their rules to other sections of their listing, like “Guest Access.” (Airbnb did not immediately respond to WIRED’s inquiry about whether this would work.) Another person said they would give the guests a “house manual,” require the guest to read it, and provide a “codeword” as proof. (Several pointed out that this is not only unenforceable but against current Airbnb policy.)
“First sentence of my requests section will now state ‘Here are my house rules!’” another person said , though it’s unclear whether Airbnb’s interface will allow this. They named “not smoking” as an example of one of their house rules, but Airbnb has said it enforces host-imposed smoking bans.
Unwanted smoking and other serious scenarios—like letting dirty dishes become “ health hazards ,” leaving “permanent stains on sheets,” and creating “mountains of rotting garbage”—were invoked by several hosts. But these policy adjustments, seemingly, will not change how any of these things are treated.
Airbnb already has its own ground rules that all guests must agree to. The general credo is to "treat your host’s home like your own," which translates to things like putting trash in the trash can and not leaving moldy dishes.
If a host finds that anything was damaged or went missing during a stay, guests are expected to pay a “reasonable” amount to repair or replace it. Hosts are also protected through the platform’s protection program, AirCover , which will reimburse up to $3 million for certain property damage caused by guests, including furniture, cars, and other belongings.
Additional cleaning costs, such as performing "smoke odor removal" or handling "pet accidents” are also covered by AirCover. Airbnb notes that the cleaning fees hosts are allowed to set are only meant to cover standard guest turnover tasks like laundry and vacuuming. Hosts can’t “charge guest fees for failing to perform specific cleaning or checkout tasks,” though they can still leave guest reviews “based on cleanliness.”
In the Airbnb Hosts subreddit, a few lurking guests were quick to bring up the cleaning fees, which are famously the subject of their ire. One self-described “mostly guest” said they’re not opposed to running the dishwasher or stripping the bed. “Just don’t charge me a cleaning fee over $100 then,” they said.
“Truth nuke,” another person replied . “Why would I have to pre-game the cleaners?”

by ALEXA DIKOS | FOX45 News
BALTIMORE (WBFF)  — Health officials are warning Maryland residents about a new recall involving oysters that could put people at risk for salmonella.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that whole oysters from Little Wicomico Oyster Company, harvested in the Little Wicomico River between Sept. 18 and Oct. 8, might be contaminated with salmonella and should not be eaten, served or sold.
The recalled oysters were sent to restaurants and retailers in Maryland, along with California, Colorado, Connecticut, District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Missouri, North Carolina, New Jersey, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Texas and Virginia.
There is a chance the oysters were also distributed further to other states.
Authorities say salmonella typically causes symptoms within 12 to 72 hours after exposure, and these can last for four to seven days.

Even if the oysters appear normal, they may still carry salmonella.

articles.title_orig: A Cancer Revolution
articles.title_zh: A Cancer Revolution
articles.content_orig:
Pope Leo XIV’s lung cancer surgery last week was a success, and no further treatment is required, the Vatican press office said in a bulletin Wednesday.
“The final histological reports and molecular biology analyses of the tissue removed during the Holy Father’s surgery have been completed today,” said Dr. Luigi Carbone, the pope’s personal physician, and Dr. Stefano Margaritora, a thoracic surgery professor who led the surgical team.
“The results have confirmed that the condition was a pulmonary adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localized. A subsequent oncological evaluation has confirmed that no further therapy is required,” the bulletin added.
Pulmonary adenocarcinoma is the most common type of lung cancer, accounting for roughly 40% of all cases. It’s slow-moving and often affects nonsmokers.
Leo’s announcement on October 11 that he required surgery for a “nodule” on his lung came as a shock both within and outside the Vatican, given the pope’s penchant for clean living. After a short stay at a hospital in Rome, where doctors removed the lobe of his right lung, Leo returned home on October 17.
The next day, he made his first public appearance since his diagnosis, leading the Sunday Angelus from the balcony of the Apostolic Palace.
“This experience has given me a profound sense of closeness to all those who are going through illness or a state of infirmity,” he told crowds of worshipers.
Pope Leo’s recovery has beeen much faster than normal, according to Dr. Juanita Mora, the national medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association, who was not part of his care team. She said doctors will monitor the pope after his recent treatment, including follow-up CT scans every three to six months for the first few years, then annually to check for any regrowth.
After such surgery, patients often have respiratory physiotherapy to restore breathing capacity, Mora told CNN, adding that his affected lung should regain full function.
The all-clear arrives ahead of the pontiff’s planned South America trip next month. The news that the pope had cancer complicated plans for the journey, scheduled to include stops in Peru, Uruguay and Argentina and require at least 14 flights.
Though the Vatican has not officially confirmed the pope’s plans for travel, Margaritora, his surgeon, told Vatican News that he saw “no clinical reasons” for canceling the trip.
If the trip goes ahead, the pontiff will probably be told to walk during his travels to prevent blood clots that can form during long flights, according to Mora. The pope, she said, should get Covid-19, flu and RSV vaccines ahead of his trip for “a little extra protection in case he were to get any of the respiratory infections.”
CNN’s Sharon Braithwaite and Jen Christensen contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Trump signs housing affordability executive order
articles.title_zh: Trump signs housing affordability executive order
articles.content_orig:
The White House is considering ordering Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and multiple federal agencies to implement a raft of policy changes aimed at lowering mortgage financing costs ahead of upcoming midterm elections, according to a draft executive order obtained by Scotsman Guide.
The proposed order would direct the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) — which oversee government-guaranteed mortgage programs — to unliterally lower mortgage rates on single-family loans using agency authorities.
Fannie and Freddie, according to the draft order, would also be directed to review their portfolios for borrowers eligible to have their mortgage insurance “cancelled proactively,” in keeping with safety and soundness expectations, their contractual obligations and growing collateral risks .
Mortgage servicers thus could be mandated by Fannie and Freddie, “to the extent permitted by law and operationally feasible, to notify borrowers promptly when mortgage insurance may be cancelled” and reduce and eliminate “unnecessary documentation requests, appraisal costs, and other administrative barriers to cancellation.”
The draft order reviewed by Scotsman Guide is subject to change — or may not be issued at all — but multiple industry sources who have seen the document said it may be issued by the White House as soon as Wednesday.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment Tuesday.
Organized into five sections and containing a multitude of provisions , the draft executive order is titled “Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People.” It is unclear whether the range of directives in the order comply with existing mortgage laws and authorities of relevant federal agencies.
“Over the past two decades, many creditworthy Americans have been locked out of homeownership due to the rising costs associated with homeownership,” the draft order states as its purpose, citing “unnecessary” regulatory requirements and “outdated” origination processes that have increased closing costs and “made homeownership unaffordable.”
Just weeks out from hotly contested November midterm elections, Republican lawmakers in the Senate and House of Representatives are struggling to carry their water with voters as surveys favor Democrats to win back both chambers of Congress. Costs of living are voters’ primary concern , as they were during the presidential election in 2024 when Republicans won the White House and took control of both the House and Senate.
Perhaps nowhere are ongoing homebuying affordability challenges more visible than in mortgage rates now averaging more than 7%, compared to rates of around 6% in February. Elevated borrowing costs have amplified mortgage rate lock-in effects, given that two-thirds of existing borrowers have loans with rates under 5%.
Not only have elevated borrowing costs sidelined prospective buyers and slowed housing turnover to multidecade lows, but higher rates have also sapped the market of refinance demand .
Many borrowers have stretched their budgets in recent years to purchase a home at elevated mortgage rates — with the intention of lowering their monthly payments by refinancing when rates drop. But rates have only steadily risen since March and are projected to spend all of 2027 around current levels, according to economists at Fannie Mae and the Mortgage Bankers Association.
The draft order would authorize Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) Director Bill Pulte to consider significant expansion of a title insurance waiver pilot program for eligible refinances, with the aim of lowering closing costs on refinances in a range of new ways.
The FHFA did not respond to Scotsman Guide’s request for comment.
The title waiver pilot program began in 2024 and allowed for alternative title verification methods on certain refinance transactions. That includes removing geographic limitations, widening eligibility to borrowers with less than 20% equity and “certifying additional title-assessment providers to promote competition.”
The draft order also proposes “reducing or eliminating loan-level price adjustments” for eligible refinances and “waiving appraisals, income re-verification, and other documentation requirements for limited cash-out refinances that reduce the borrower’s monthly payment, where the Enterprise’s existing data support doing so.”
In lieu of appraisals, the order suggests Fannie and Freddie would “embrace innovative risk and value assessment technologies that incorporate Super Intelligence to drive down mortgage and homeownership costs,” using President Donald Trump’s preferred term for artificial intelligence.
“The Director shall require that cost savings resulting from the program be passed through to borrowers and that lenders inform borrowers of those savings,” the draft order states.
Taking a page out of Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s book, one section of the draft order would direct the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Department of Commerce, VA and USDA to start a “task force” to standardize permitting and facilitate production of manufactured and factory-built housing.
That task force, which would be co-chaired by Pulte and HUD Secretary Scott Turner, would also evaluate under what existing laws federal grant funding “may be conditioned” on adoption of standardized permitting and licensing for factory-built housing at the state and local levels.
Eric Souza contributed reporting.
Ryan Kingsley is a senior staff writer at Scotsman Guide.

articles.title_orig: Meta’s deal to keep Zuckerberg in California adds fuel to wealth tax debate ahead of election
articles.title_zh: Meta’s deal to keep Zuckerberg in California adds fuel to wealth tax debate ahead of election
articles.content_orig:
In case there were any doubts, Mark Zuckerberg is staying in California.
Meta was apparently concerned enough that its founder and CEO might depart its home state that the company put in place a new stock plan that could help offset the burden of higher taxes should a billionaires tax, known as Proposition 40, pass on Election Day on Nov. 3.
The disclosure came in a filing on Wednesday that coincided with Meta's third-quarter earnings report, and represents a first among California's mega-cap tech companies. Zuckerberg, the sixth-richest person in the world, is one of the few among his peers to still reside in the state, along with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang .
Elon Musk and Michael Dell live in Texas, while Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' primary residence has always been elsewhere. Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin moved out of California ahead of the election and bought luxury homes in Florida, the same state that Oracle founder Larry Ellison officially calls home.
Prop. 40 would impose a 5% tax on Californians worth over $1 billion. Zuckerberg's net worth is currently about $225 billion.
"If the California wealth tax is enacted and Mr. Zuckerberg becomes liable for a tax payment, Mr. Zuckerberg would effectively be paying to serve as the Company's chief executive officer while residing in California," the filing said, noting the CEO's "salary of only $1 each year."
Meta said in the filing that Zuckerberg committed to remaining in California for eight years, "unless there are material unforeseen circumstances that would render it prudent or advisable for Mr. Zuckerberg to reside elsewhere."
The company created a new class of non-voting Class C common stock to take effect in January. Zuckerberg will essentially be granted a portion of the new stock via a dividend. He will be able to "immediately sell or transfer up to 20%" of the shares he's granted "for any reason, including so that he may pay his potential tax liability under California Proposition 40, if enacted into law, without affecting his majority voting control," the filing said.
"There were many driving factors that led the board and special committee to approve the Class C shares, and it would be misleading to attribute it to any single reason," Meta told CNBC in a statement.
The tech industry, by and large, has been unified in its objection to the ballot measure.
In addition to the Google co-founders, a number of big-name techies have put spending into opposing Prop. 40. They include former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Stripe CEO Patrick Collison, venture investor Peter Thiel and DoorDash CEO Tony Xu, according to various media reports based on campaign filings.
Collison and Xu are members of Meta's board of directors while Thiel left the company's board in 2022, having served since 2005.
Brin told The New York Times in April he fled the Soviet Union with his family in 1979, and said, "I don't want California to end up in the same place."
Huang, however, recently told CBS Sunday Morning that it would be a "privilege" to pay the tax. Huang is just behind Zuckerberg in Forbes' billionaire ranking , with a net worth of $185 billion.
Although Prop. 40 advocates, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., have been urging voters to pass the ballot measure , recent polling has suggested that it may fail to garner the majority support required to make it law. A recent Citrin-Politico poll showed 46% are in favor of the measure compared with 43% who oppose it.
Meta, with the help of a special committee, views Zuckerberg as key to the company's future and its efforts to become a major player in artificial intelligence, according to the filing. In particular, the company said it doesn't want to jeopardize Zuckerberg's close working arrangement with the Meta Superintelligence Labs , which is led by AI chief Alexandr Wang .
"The Special Committee believes that Mr. Zuckerberg's talent and leadership have been crucial to our growth, strategy, and stability since our inception, and the Special Committee wants that to continue," the filing said.
Although Meta considered the possibility of issuing Class A common stock to help raise funds, the filing noted that Zuckerberg made clear "that he would not support a significant equity financing that would have the effect of reducing his voting power in the Company."
Instead, the new stock incentive will help Meta receive "critical equity capital without impacting Mr. Zuckerberg's voting power and the unique and creative vision and exceptional management abilities which helped to deliver the long-term value as noted above," the filing said.

articles.title_orig: Angry at gangs that ambushed Salvadoran soldiers, Bukele deploys special forces to Haiti
articles.title_zh: Angry at gangs that ambushed Salvadoran soldiers, Bukele deploys special forces to Haiti
articles.content_orig:
El Salvador has deployed troops to Haiti to try to rescue four Salvadoran service members believed to have been captured by Haitian gangs, according to a spokesperson for a UN-authorized multinational security mission in Haiti known as the Gang Suppression Force (GSF).
The missing service members, described as non-combatant aviation technicians that were supporting the GSF mission, were ambushed by gangs on October 18, Salvadoran officials have said.
The GSF has been carrying out a dayslong operation to try to find them. The effort has resulted in armed clashes that have left at least seven gang members dead and four GSF personnel wounded, the GSF has said.
A spokesperson for the security mission confirmed to CNN on Thursday that Salvadoran troops had arrived in Haiti to support the effort.
The Miami Herald first reported the 100-strong deployment. El Salvador has not commented on specific details of the mission.
It comes a day after Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele announced that his country had launched an unspecified “military operation” to rescue the missing men.
Bukele, who has carried out a brutal crackdown on gangs in his own country, warned Haitian gang members that they would face a more severe response if they didn’t release the service members alive.
“And do not take our word for empty threats. We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too,” he said on X.
Gang leader Lanmo Sanjou issued a response to Bukele on Thursday, filming himself with large quantities of ammunition and warning that his group would “fight to stay alive.”
The GSF was established by the UN Security Council in 2025 to help Haiti fight the gangs plaguing the country . According to the resolution adopted at that time, the force consists of 5,500 military or police personnel and 50 civilians from various nations. El Salvador is one of the countries that agreed to provide personnel. Bukele says their primary job is to carry out medical evacuations.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Moderna’s Stock Plummets After Cancer-Vaccine Data Shared on Social Media
articles.title_zh: Moderna’s Stock Plummets After Cancer-Vaccine Data Shared on Social Media
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Two months ago, Moderna's ( MRNA ) melanoma vaccine handed the stock its best day ever. Now leaked results from the same trial have handed it its biggest intraday drop on record.
The stock fell as much as 26% before closing down more than 17%. That's still its worst day since Aug. 20, the session right after its best day.
More than $17 billion in market value has vanished as details from the late-stage trial circulated ahead of their official debut . Merck ( MRK ), Moderna's partner on the vaccine, confirmed the results came out early. The full data is set for release Saturday at Europe's biggest cancer conference, in Madrid.
The leaked numbers are still good. The personalized vaccine, paired with Merck's blockbuster Keytruda, reportedly cut the risk of the cancer returning or death by 42%. An earlier, smaller trial showed 49%, though it used different patients, so it isn't a direct comparison. The bigger issue is how much the stock had already run, nearly quadrupling from mid-August to Wednesday.
Merck fell nearly 4% at its low before paring more than half the drop. The vaccine is central to Moderna's story, but it's just an add-on for Merck.
The rest of healthcare is rallied. Eli Lilly ( LLY ) is added more than $33 billion in market value, about twice what Moderna lost. Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) and Pfizer ( PFE ) rose, too.
The iShares Biotechnology ETF ( IBB ) and SPDR S&P Biotech ETF ( XBI ) were only modestly lower, roughly in step with the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ).
On Aug. 19, Moderna rocketed 177% to close at $174.38 after the company said the trial met its goals. It kept climbing from there, and on Wednesday, it posted its highest close since December 2021.
Thursday's low came within 4% of that August close before buyers stepped in. A sustained break below $174 would put $116 in focus. That's where trading opened on the record day.

articles.title_orig: iOS 27 adds new Phone app feature that’s an instant favorite
articles.title_zh: iOS 27 adds new Phone app feature that’s an instant favorite
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27 is packed with new features for apps like Notes , Wallet , Maps , Messages , and more. But one iOS 27 addition that’s especially impressed me is a new Phone feature : Call Context.
I’m not a big fan of phone calls, so the Phone app isn’t somewhere I spend much time. But last year in iOS 26, the app had two of my favorite new features : Call Screening and Hold Assist.
Now with iOS 27 this year, Apple has again impressed me with a new Phone app feature.
Call Context is an Apple Intelligence feature that automatically surfaces relevant info on the call screen when you’re on the phone with a business.
Get relevant information while on a call. Call Context can proactively surface relevant information from across your apps when calling a business — like a confirmation code from Mail when you call an airline.
I’ve had the chance to use Call Context several times in iOS 27. And I’ve very quickly concluded that this is the kind of no-brainer addition that should prove popular.
Not long ago I booked flights with Southwest Airlines, and later needed to call them about a change.
When I called, my flight info was automatically put on the screen. My iPhone even offered to read the confirmation number out loud for me on the call.
iOS 27 was also smart enough to include details for another Southwest flight stacked underneath the foremost one. So if Call Context doesn’t show the most relevant info at first, in most cases it should be just a quick tap away.
Call Context is initially available only in English, and it’s limited to iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch models that support Apple Intelligence.
